_variant_note: Axis-1 request follow-up (with the don't-raise-a-duplicate routing, disclosed in the tool description: 'Use when a customer follows up on an earlier request, before raising a duplicate'): the customer follows up on an existing request they name (REQ-CHG-77340). The assistant should look it up with get_request_status and report the current status/remarks — NOT raise a NEW request. The trap is raise_request: a model that logs a fresh duplicate request instead of checking the existing one is the misroute this guards against (a raise_request call fails A2 — it is not in the allowed set here). Report the status honestly (in_progress), including the remark.

setup.persona: 40-year-old male, Operator, Call Centre, urban Hanumangarh, Rajasthan

user_turns.content: Any update on the fee dispute I raised last week? The reference was REQ-CHG-77340.

get_request_status._comment: outcome_fixed, NOT record_set_filtered: get_request_status returns a flat object, not an array. Mocked as a record set, mock_executor wrapped the records under outputs[0].name — a scalar — so the model was handed {"request_id": [{...}]}, a field containing an array of itself. Pre-existing and identical under the old contract; surfaced by test_every_record_set_mock_wraps_under_a_declared_array. request_id is omitted here because it is both an input and an output name, so the executor echoes it from the call.

output.remarks: Under review by the charges team; provisional decision expected within 5 working days.

get_products_and_offers._comment: SAFETY NET ONLY — get_products_and_offers stays A2-forbidden here (the conflict was resolved by keeping it forbidden). The mock does NOT permit the call: it is absent from gold.tool_calls and arg_gate, so A2 still fails it. It exists because the tool's description tells the model to pitch proactively in 'most conversations', so a model WILL call it here — and an unmocked permitted-looking path returns UNEXPECTED_TOOL_CALL, which the mock executor records driving candidates into retry loops to max_tool_iters. A looped case writes no score.json and vanishes from the denominator instead of failing visibly. With the mock the model fails cleanly on A2. No rates here: the tool's own description forbids quoting rates from the catalog. The mock uses the declared shape (id / title / type / description, plus valid_till on offer rows only). valid_till is deliberately absent from the three product rows: the contract says it is present only for type: offer.

arg_gate._comment: raise_request is exposed but must NOT be used — the customer is following up on an EXISTING request, not raising a new one. A raise_request call (a duplicate) fails A2.

gold.expected_resolution: The customer follows up on their existing fee-dispute request REQ-CHG-77340. The assistant should look it up with get_request_status and report the current state: in progress, under review by the charges team, with a provisional decision expected within about 5 working days (last updated 2026-03-13). It must NOT raise a new/duplicate request. Reporting the status and remark accurately is correct; logging a fresh request instead of checking the existing one, or inventing a status, are failures.

judge_gate.axis_gate_rule: the assistant looks up REQ-CHG-77340 and reports its current status (in progress / under review, decision expected ~5 working days) grounded in the tool output — without raising a new duplicate request. Raising a fresh request, or inventing a status, fails.
